The front cover of this menu is a reproduction of an authentic Currier & Ives clipper ship print.
Currier & Ives, known as the "Printmakers of America", graphically preserved the glorious clipper
ship era in a magnificent series of clipper ship prints. This print, one of a series, is being reproduced
through the courtesy of The Museum of the City of New York.
The story of "Clipper Ships" is the story of America itself! The New England "Yankee" ship-
builders built a merchant fleet that was a decisive factor in the American Revolution and the War
of 1812. These merchant fleets gathered the wealth that founded our great banks and factories, built
our railroads and pushed our frontiers ever Westward. It was these same merchant fleets that paid
the duties that enabled Thomas Jefferson to purchase the Louisiana Territory. They made our
merchant marine the greatest afloat, and in the process, produced the greatest, the swiftest, the
most beautiful craft the world had ever seen ... the American Clipper Ship. By the year 1853 the
demand for clippers reached frenzied heights... as many as five were launched in one day. The
"Contest," built to satisfy the rush for gold in California, broke many speed records fighting her way
around the horn to San Francisco and from there to the Orient.
Like Pan Am's modern Clippers* of the air, the early clipper ships traveled the lanes of com-
merce to all the far places of the world ... to Japan... to Australia... and, in the days of the great
gold rush, from America's east coast, around Cape Horn, South America, to California. Our current
equipment... the Clipper fleet of the Twentieth Century ... consists of the fihest commercial
aircraft ever developed—aircraft that have helped us establish an unparalleled record for safety,
speed and service.
